global_organization_chain: summary states the claim and withholds the numbers
introduction renames the problem from loose to precise and lists the work
assumptions fix what the strategy is allowed to do
preprocessing makes the two series comparable
the model turns a cointegration result into a trading rule
the results beat three baselines and name a stable parameter window
the sensitivity section reads one cost figure two ways
the conclusion answers the four problem questions one subsection each
strengths and improvements judge the work
the memorandum retells it to the trader in the second person

moves: input: the two assets and the requirement to trade on prices known that day
rhetorical job: state the conclusion before any number, then spend five blocks earning it
analytical job: report the terminal value, the three multiplier ranges, the cost findings and the risk split
output: a six-block summary with the claim in block 1 and the numbers in blocks 2 to 5
handoff: the final block points at the memorandum instead of adding a result
section_progressions.positive_pattern: state the conclusion before any number, then spend five blocks earning it

moves: input: a reader who has not been told which two assets matter
rhetorical job: withhold the first person until section 1.2 and concede gold's case before ranking bitcoin
analytical job: name the problem twice, loose then precise, and list four work items
output: three background paragraphs, one method paragraph and four non-parallel bullets
handoff: the last bullet hands risk to section 6 and the lead sentence of section 2 opens the assumptions
section_progressions.positive_pattern: withhold the first person until section 1.2 and concede gold's case before ranking bitcoin

moves: input: the four work items just promised
rhetorical job: put each assumption and its reason inside the same bullet
analytical job: fix history-repeats, no delay, no leverage and close-price settlement
output: four bullets, one of them excluding leverage because unlimited leverage would make the study meaningless
handoff: section 3 opens on the data the assumptions just licensed
section_progressions.positive_pattern: put each assumption and its reason inside the same bullet

moves: input: two raw price series with mismatched calendars
rhetorical job: let each Therefore point back at the test result just stated
analytical job: test stationarity, fill gold's missing days with the previous valid price, normalize by L2
output: a cleaned, normalized series and the decision to keep the original data
handoff: section 4 reads the normalized figure and starts guessing at a relationship
section_progressions.positive_pattern: let each Therefore point back at the test result just stated

moves: input: the normalized prices and a suspected lag
rhetorical job: move from a general definition down to the case in hand, then restate it in plain words
analytical job: test cointegration, define the pairs rules, the deviation, the two constraints and the risk interval
output: the MDN trading rule plus the non-trading interval and the risk-aversion utility
handoff: section 5 takes the rule as given and builds the baselines to beat it
section_progressions.positive_pattern: move from a general definition down to the case in hand, then restate it in plain words

moves: input: one proposed strategy and three baselines
rhetorical job: open the section with a one-sentence roadmap and gloss each metric before its formula
analytical job: compare on return, volatility, geometric return, Jensen, Sharpe, information ratio and tracking error, then vary the lag
output: two ranking lines, a stable lag window of 15 to 60 days, and a terminal value
handoff: the conclusion's three adjectives are what section 8.1.2 repeats
section_progressions.positive_pattern: open the section with a one-sentence roadmap and gloss each metric before its formula

moves: input: the transaction cost the strategy pays on every trade
rhetorical job: picture the fee as an intercept, then read one figure in two directions
analytical job: derive the asset value after n trades and plot return against cost
output: a negative relationship read once as promotion and once as inhibition
handoff: section 8.1.3 compresses the same relationship into one sentence with and vice versa
section_progressions.positive_pattern: picture the fee as an intercept, then read one figure in two directions

moves: input: the terminal value, the comparison and the sensitivity result
rhetorical job: give each of the four problem questions its own numbered subsection
analytical job: restate the value, the multiples against two rivals, the cost correlation and the memo's location
output: four short subsections, one of them a single sentence pointing at the memorandum
handoff: section 8.2 and 8.3 turn from results to judgement
section_progressions.positive_pattern: give each of the four problem questions its own numbered subsection

moves: input: the finished model and the things it left out
rhetorical job: stack three judgements in one strength bullet and give exclusions a reason about clarity
analytical job: claim scientific basis, profitability and decision support; name richer assets, statistical learning and leverage as future work
output: three strength bullets and three improvement bullets
handoff: the memorandum repeats the strengths for a reader who skips the paper
section_progressions.positive_pattern: stack three judgements in one strength bullet and give exclusions a reason about clarity

moves: input: a trader who has not read the paper
rhetorical job: switch to the second person, decline machine learning out of caution, and close with an imperative
analytical job: restate the cointegration basis, the backtest safeguard and three indicators with the strategy's own numbers
output: a letter with a four-line header, three bullets and a sales closing line
handoff: none; the memo is the last thing the trader reads
section_progressions.positive_pattern: switch to the second person, decline machine learning out of caution, and close with an imperative

main_argument_chains.claim: The pairs strategy beats the baselines because gold and bitcoin are cointegrated.
support_steps: The normalized prices show bitcoin lagging gold, so a relationship is guessed.
The Johansen test finds a lagging cointegration, which the paper says lays the foundation.
The pairs rule buys the asset below its equilibrium and sells the one above.
Against random, XGBoost and LSTM baselines the strategy leads on return and on Sharpe.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The trader is told to use the pairs rule rather than a machine-learning model.

main_argument_chains.claim: The terminal wealth is reported three different ways and the paper never reconciles them.
support_steps: The summary turns $1,000 into $106,986.1 on September 10, 2021.
Section 5.5 and section 8.1.1 print $106,686.1 on October 9, 2021.
The memorandum prints $106986.1 with no thousands separator, dated September 10, 2021.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: No single terminal value can be quoted without saying which page it came from.

main_argument_chains.claim: Transaction cost lowers return, and the paper shows it twice.
support_steps: The summary states a negative exponential relationship and a zero-cost theoretical endpoint of $120000.
Section 7 derives asset value after n trades and reads one figure as both promotion and inhibition.
Section 8.1.3 compresses the relationship to one sentence and says and vice versa.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The trader is warned that raising the commission shrinks the gain.

main_argument_chains.claim: Risk is handled by not trading, not by hedging.
support_steps: Market risk is split into price risk and reinvestment risk.
A non-trading interval is defined and the strategy holds cash while the forecast sits inside it.
A risk-aversion coefficient rescales the utility, so different investors hold different cash.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The strategy answers risk by holding cash rather than by adding leverage, which assumption 3 already forbids.

model_retention.equation_free_boundary: All four retained models carry equations; none were invented to fill a gap.

visualization_dispositions.analytical_purpose: Show the two raw price series before any processing, so the reader sees the scale difference the normalization later removes.
Show both return distributions are sharply centered at zero before the stationarity argument.
Justify differencing by showing the autocorrelation dies after the first difference.
Show how gold's missing market days are filled, so the reader sees the rule rather than only reading it.
Make the lag visible so the cointegration test that follows has something to confirm.
Show the pairs rule acting, with the buy and sell marks the prose legend names.
Argue the engineered features separate and are not redundant before the machine-learning baselines.
Show the pairwise shape of three features the prose treats as representative.
Show the leakage safeguard and the model the baselines use, before any result is claimed.
Put the four strategies' net worth on one axis so the gap is visible before the tables quantify it.
Give the two basic indicators as numbers so the two ranking lines that follow can be checked.
Add the four developed indicators so the summary's multiplier ranges have a source.
Show the tracking error over time so the prose can dismiss the 2017 spike as one period.
Show the terminal value against the lag so the stable window has a picture.
Restate the terminal comparison as bars so the gap reads at a glance.
Show return against time for ten cost rates so the cost effect is a family of curves.
Give the cost effect a closed form and a fitted curve.
Restate the terminal result as a before-and-after for the conclusion.
Repeat the comparison in the conclusion so section 8.1.2's multiples have a figure.
Repeat the sensitivity figures inside the conclusion so problem 3 has its own picture.
Show the trader the safeguard the prose calls separation from the data.
Repeat the comparison for the reader who only reads the memorandum.
Name the software and versions behind the results.
State how each of the four strategies was built.

warnings.precise_source_claim: The trace statistic has one sample-size symbol.
warnings.warning: Equation (4) prints n in front of the sum and N as the upper limit, and the gloss defines only N. The skill may teach the statistic with one symbol. It must not copy both.

warnings.precise_source_claim: The rule trades against an equilibrium price.
warnings.warning: Equation (7) averages two returns, and the prose calls the result the equilibrium price. The skill may teach a mean return used as a reference. It must not teach that average as a price.

warnings.precise_source_claim: Past returns are defined by a displayed formula.
warnings.warning: Equation (12) falls under the page-11 running header and no pixels of it survive at 100 dpi, so it was transcribed from the text layer at medium confidence. The skill may teach the definition as unverified. It must not teach it as visually confirmed.
Equation (11) is introduced by the printed placeholder 'features(??)'. The skill may teach a feature list that is written out. It must not teach a placeholder as a list.

warnings.precise_source_claim: Tracking error measures how far a strategy strays.
warnings.warning: Equation (22) sets TE = E(r'_p) - r_f with no volatility in the denominator, and the gloss writes the prime in a different place from the formula. The skill may teach a tracking error with a spread in the denominator. It must not teach this definition as that measure.

warnings.precise_source_claim: The geometric return compounds the daily returns.
warnings.warning: Equation (18) is printed with a product, which the text layer read as a sum. The skill may teach the product. It must not restore the sum the text layer suggests.

warnings.precise_source_claim: One risk-aversion coefficient links the information ratio to the utility.
warnings.warning: Equation (28) divides by 2*phi_p while equation (29) squares phi_p, and the paper never connects the two. The skill may teach either form and mark the other as printed differently. It must not teach them as one consistent derivation.

The summary states $120000 with no thousands separator, and none of equations (30) to (33) produce it. The skill may teach the closed form. It must not teach $120000 as the value the closed form gives.

warnings.precise_source_claim: The cost formula in the figure is the cost formula in the text.
warnings.warning: Equation (33) carries the exponent n, while the boxed formula in Figure 16 panel (b) carries 25. The skill may teach the displayed equation. It must not teach the boxed 25 as the same expression.

fact_notation_claim_warnings.precise_source_claim: The strategy turns the initial cash into a stated terminal value.
fact_notation_claim_warnings.warning: Three terminal values are printed and never reconciled: the summary gives $106,986.1 on September 10, 2021; sections 5.5 and 8.1.1 give $106,686.1 on October 9, 2021; the memorandum and Figure 17 give $106986.1 with no thousands separator, dated September 10, 2021. The skill may teach that a result must carry its page. It must not quote any one of these as the result.

fact_notation_claim_warnings.precise_source_claim: The growth is called nearly 107 times year-on-year.
fact_notation_claim_warnings.warning: 106986.1 divided by 1000 is about 106.99, and the window is five years, not one. The skill may teach a total multiple over a stated window. It must not teach 'year-on-year' for a five-year total.

fact_notation_claim_warnings.precise_source_claim: The data window is a single stated interval.
fact_notation_claim_warnings.warning: The summary dates it September 10, 2016 to September 10, 2021; section 3.1.1 dates the start November 9, 2016; sections 5.5 and 8.1.1 date the end October 9, 2021. The skill may teach one window named once. It must not merge these into a single interval.

fact_notation_claim_warnings.precise_source_claim: The strategy beats the baselines by the ranges given in the summary.
fact_notation_claim_warnings.warning: Section 8.1.2 prints a third set, 24.87 times the random strategy and 8.03 times XGBoost, beside the summary's 1.53-2.32, 1.49-3.17 and 1.63-3.25. The skill may teach each set with its page and its baseline. It must not treat them as the same comparison.

fact_notation_claim_warnings.precise_source_claim: The rule opens a position when the gap exceeds a threshold.
fact_notation_claim_warnings.warning: Algorithm 1 prints the comparison with an empty right-hand side, 'if R~_A - R_B > then'. The skill may teach a rule whose threshold is named and valued. It must not teach a trigger with nothing on the right.

fact_notation_claim_warnings.precise_source_claim: Transaction cost both promotes and inhibits return.
fact_notation_claim_warnings.warning: Section 7 reads one figure as a promotion effect and an inhibition effect of the same cost. The skill may teach one negative relationship described twice. It must not teach cost as both a promotion and an inhibition.

fact_notation_claim_warnings.precise_source_claim: The interval in which the strategy holds cash has one name.
fact_notation_claim_warnings.warning: The summary calls it the non-investable interval and section 6.1.2 calls it the non-trading interval. The skill may teach one term. It must not use both for one interval.

fact_notation_claim_warnings.precise_source_claim: The scatter matrix is the figure the prose points to.
fact_notation_claim_warnings.warning: The prose says 'as can be seen from Figure 10' for the scatter matrix, which is printed as Figure 8. The skill may teach a cross-reference that names the figure it means. It must not cite Figure 10 for this plot.

gate_attestation.warning_boundary: Last pass only; no positive evidence derived from warnings.
